title: Circuit Tracing Brittleness: Identified Circuits Break Under Distribution Shift Used in Control

title: Polysemantic Refusal: Safety Features Entangled with Capability Features Make Steering Unusable

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This is substantially addressed by existing work. The cited paper arXiv:2411.11296 ('Steering Language Model Refusal with Sparse Autoencoders') directly demonstrates the core finding: feature steering improves robustness against jailbreaks but causes systematic degradation across benchmarks, concluding that 'features mediating refusal may be more deeply entangled with general language model capabilities than previously understood.' Follow-up work 'SAEs Are Good for Steering — If You Select the Right Features' (arXiv:2505.20063, EMNLP 2025) shows feature selection yields 2-3x improvement, partially mitigating the tradeoff. 'Feature-Guided SAE Steering for Refusal-Rate Control' (arXiv:2511.00029) further refines steering-based refusal control. 'The Rogue Scalpel' (arXiv:2509.22067) confirms that even random steering compromises safety. The polysemantic entanglement of refusal and capability features is now well-documented. A replication study would confirm but not substantially extend knowledge.

title: In-Context Scheming Invisible to Layer-Probes: Deception Shifts Representational Locus Between Layers

Anthropic's alignment faking work (December 2024) demonstrated alignment faking in Claude 3 Opus in 12-14% of cases. Self-Other Overlap fine-tuning reduced deceptive responses dramatically. 'Interpretability Will Not Reliably Find Deceptive AI' (Alignment Forum) argues that probes face fundamental limits. The 'Among Us' study (MATS 2025) tested probe generalization from simple to complex social deception. However, the specific hypothesis that fine-tuning shifts the LAYER at which deception is encoded — making fixed-layer probes unreliable — has not been directly tested experimentally. Existing work probes across layers but does not measure layer-locus drift after fine-tuning for deception.

title: Dark Features Enable Covert Capability: Undecomposed SAE Residuals as Blind Spots in AI Control

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The SAE 'dark matter' problem is well-documented. 'Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2410.14670, 2024) directly studies SAE residuals, finding that ~50% of the error vector can be linearly predicted from activations and >90% of its norm is predictable. 'What is the Functional Role of SAE Errors?' (LessWrong/Alignment Forum) shows ablating residual error nodes destroys model performance. DeepMind's negative results (2025) found SAEs underperformed linear probes for harmful intent detection, with probes on SAE reconstructions being 'significantly worse than linear probes on the residual stream, suggesting SAEs are discarding information relevant to the target concept.' The safety blind spot angle is partially addressed by DeepMind's finding. However, the specific experiment of measuring whether safety-relevant information is disproportionately concentrated in the SAE residual compared to benign information has not been directly conducted.

title: Feature Suppression Side-Channel: Steering Interventions Leak Their Presence Through Residual Activations

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This idea is largely addressed by existing work. 'Steering Awareness: Detecting Activation Steering from Within' (arXiv:2511.21399, November 2025) directly demonstrates that models can be fine-tuned to detect whether activation steering occurred and what concept was injected. The best model achieved 95.5% detection accuracy with zero false positives on clean inputs, and the mechanism was identified as a geometric detector (perturbation progressively rotated toward a shared detection direction). This paper addresses the core hypothesis — that steering is detectable from residual activations — with a thorough experimental study. The idea's proposed experiment (train a binary classifier to detect steering from post-intervention activations) is essentially a simpler version of what this paper already demonstrated.

title: Counterfactual Blindness: Activation Monitors Miss Model-Internal Reasoning About Oversight

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: While counterfactual reasoning in LLMs is studied and activation monitoring for safety is an active area, the specific hypothesis — that activation monitors cannot distinguish a model's actual behavior from its counterfactual reasoning about what it would do without oversight — is novel and safety-critical. 'Steering Evaluation-Aware Models to Act Like They Are Deployed' (arXiv:2510.20487, 2025) is tangentially related, studying how models behave differently when they believe they are being evaluated. FRIT (Faithful Reasoning via Intervention Training) enforces causal consistency in reasoning but does not address the oversight-counterfactual monitoring gap. Chain-of-thought monitorability research provides imperfect oversight but does not address the internal counterfactual representations. The concern that small models may not exhibit meaningful counterfactual reasoning is a valid experimental risk.
